doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Leading groups in Philadelphia and Air Force musicians
summary: He led groups in the Air Force and a trio in Philadelphia with Jimmy Heath, Specs Wright and Kenny Barron, whom he met by following a bassist.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well tell me about, in Philadelphia you had some of your own band-leading experiences, didn’t you? Did you lead some of your own groups eventually?

Well I led a group in the Air Force as well. And I had a trio around Philadelphia and I worked with Jimmy Heath and Specs Wright and Sam Dochre and Kenny Barron. Did I tell you I met Kenny Barron? I saw a bass player going into the subway one day. And I says, “hey, where are you going?” He says, “I’m going to a session.” I says, “you mind if I follow you?” So he says, “no, come on.” So I followed him around and he went over this guy’s house, the guy was playing piano. It was Kenny Barron. It was Kenny’s house. And later on I discovered that Kenny worked with Heath, Jimmy Heath on the weekends. And that’s how that relationship began. And I met a lot of musicians that were on the corner that played. I met Ray Gullin in Boston and worked with him for six months. I met the chief arranger for the Air Force band in DC, we worked together for a while. And now these were all very, very, very talented people, very smart and very hard working people. And there was something about them, some qualities about them that I liked.

They had those abilities to do these things. But I discovered that it was more work than just being smart. It was a lot of work. A lot of work. Effort. And a lot of things that I didn’t necessarily want to hear, like I said, musically. I had to go through all of that in order to reach the type of sound that I wanted to reach.
